news.title: Intel Xe updates improve support for B60, B70 and Panther Lake
news.summary: Intel has made major Xe updates intended to improve gaming and LLM workloads across configurations involving Intel B60 and B70 GPUs and Panther Lake systems. The transcript describes the changes as making these setups easier to use.

news.title: Linux 7.3 reaches its fifth release candidate
news.summary: Linux 7.3-rc5 has been published, with the release cycle described as unusually large and containing many updates. The speaker said a further release candidate might be needed, with the final release estimated around October 18 or 20.

news.title: COSMIC Desktop says it will not accept AI-generated pull requests
news.summary: The COSMIC Desktop project announced that it will not accept AI pull requests. The discussion framed this as a requirement that contributors understand and take responsibility for the code they submit, even when using AI tools.

news.title: Rust 1.98.1 fixes a vtable-generation miscompilation
news.summary: An emergency Rust 1.98.1 point release addresses a miscompilation in vtable generation.

news.title: Debian 13.7 is released
news.summary: Debian 13.7 landed a few weeks before the recording. The speaker also mentioned working on a Debian system and publishing a related guide, but did not describe the release contents.

news.title: Ubuntu 26.10 beta is delayed
news.summary: The beta for Ubuntu 26.10, referred to in the transcript as “Stalking Stingray,” has been delayed. No revised beta date or reason for the delay was given.

news.title: Contributor reports a GNOME touchpad-acceleration patch made with AI assistance
news.summary: A contributor used AI assistance to develop a patch addressing a long-standing GNOME touchpad-acceleration issue. The speaker said the result was reasonable but was not part of mainline GNOME.

news.title: Testing shows dual V100 GPUs can run modern AI models at higher speeds with newer CUDA
news.summary: The speaker reported running modern models, including Qwen 3.8 8B, on dual NVIDIA V100 GPUs at about 50 tokens per second using CUDA. With the last CUDA version officially supporting the cards, the reported speed was about six to seven tokens per second, without changing quantization.

news.title: Event Horizon project adds system-event monitoring and IOC dashboard work
news.summary: The speaker reported progress on Event Horizon, a project that collects system events and is being developed with a graphical interface for lightweight indicators of compromise. A test machine had recorded 4,382 systemd-related events over roughly two and a half days of normal use.

news.title: Linux MD work targets better support for host-managed zoned drives
news.summary: The speaker is developing a version of Linux MD intended to be more aware of zoned storage and better optimized for host-managed zoned drives. The work aims to reduce write amplification and unnecessary disk-head movement while keeping metadata in the drives’ conventional recording area.

news.title: Event Horizon project resumes development as a centralized event-monitoring tool
news.summary: The creator is using a Dell Pro Max GB10 system to run tests on Event Horizon, a project intended to collect and forward events from Linux and Windows machines for centralized browsing. The early concept includes a web interface and optional small-language-model assistance for diagnosing errors such as Windows blue screens; the project is described as very beta and not yet formally announced.

news.title: Microsoft executive calls AI scraping a major theft of labor
news.summary: A Microsoft executive characterized AI scraping as the largest theft of labor in human history. The discussion frames the remark as part of the dispute over AI systems using online content.

news.title: Microsoft data reportedly shows Copilot reduced New York Times clickthrough rates by up to 93%
news.summary: The transcript cites Microsoft data indicating that its Copilot engine cut clickthrough rates to the New York Times by as much as 93%. It also says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella testified that paywalled content used for training should have been licensed.

news.title: Drone strikes reportedly caused permanent customer data loss at AWS
news.summary: The transcript reports that drone strikes caused permanent customer data loss at AWS, describing it as the second such incident. It emphasizes that AWS uptime guarantees apply to the service and do not guarantee that an individual customer’s instance or data is backed up.

news.title: Fujitsu launches a 144-core, 2nm ARM server CPU
news.summary: Fujitsu has launched a 144-core ARM server processor built on a 2nm process with 3D stacking. The transcript also cites a 3.8 GHz clock speed, 8,800 megatransfers-per-second memory, and GCC 15 compiler support.

news.title: Shell Zero Click RC plugin reportedly targets major AI coding agents
news.summary: The transcript mentions a Shell Zero Click RC plugin that affects all major AI coding agents. It provides no further details about the plugin’s behavior or impact.

news.title: Google deprecates Gemini CLI
news.summary: Google has deprecated Gemini CLI and, according to the transcript, is telling users not to use it. No replacement or migration details are given.

news.title: Zero-click attacks reportedly compromise Google Pixel phones
news.summary: The transcript reports modern zero-click attacks affecting Google Pixel phones. It characterizes the development as worrying but gives no technical details about the attacks.

news.title: GitLab users urged to update after a maximum-severity vulnerability
news.summary: The transcript warns self-hosted GitLab users to update because a vulnerability rated 10 out of 10 has already been disclosed. It suggests affected users may need to format and reinstall, but does not identify the CVE or provide remediation details.

news.title: Fedora 45 beta features GNOME 51
news.summary: The Fedora 45 beta is mentioned as a distribution release, with GNOME 51 identified as a feature. No additional release details are provided.

news.title: Ubuntu works to complete its Rust coreutils transition
news.summary: Ubuntu is described as finishing its move to Rust coreutils. The change has generated controversy, and the transcript notes the importance of preserving the accumulated knowledge and testing associated with the existing utilities.

news.title: Rust warns that key developers are being targeted for compromise
news.summary: Rust has issued a warning that key developers are being targeted for compromise, including through fake LinkedIn posts and people attempting to join projects. The transcript connects this to the growing use of advanced AI tools in adversarial activity.

news.title: Paid campaigns reportedly offer creators money to promote anti-AI sentiment
news.summary: The speaker claims that substantial money is being distributed to online creators and video makers for paid anti-AI messaging, and describes the activity as organized. The transcript does not identify the funders or provide supporting evidence.

news.title: China directs government organizations to move away from Windows
news.summary: The Chinese government has issued a directive to move away from Windows, which the speakers say is currently used in a customized Windows 10 version. Data privacy concerns, including Windows telemetry, were among the reasons discussed.

news.title: Researchers reportedly found vulnerabilities in applications distributed by LG's installer
news.summary: The speakers say researchers found vulnerabilities in what they believe was every application installable through an LG app installer. They connect this to earlier reporting about residential proxy software, but provide no details about the individual flaws.

news.title: LG firmware updates are said to restrict customization and device access
news.summary: The speakers say newer LG firmware is less tolerant of homebrew and customization, and that LG has taken steps to make devices harder to root. They also describe later firmware as more adversarial to analysis, while noting that manufacturers may respond to discovered exploits by locking devices down.

news.title: Hackers have run Alpine Linux on LG webOS devices
news.summary: The speakers report that hackers have gotten an accessible version of Alpine Linux running on webOS. They also say there is evidence modern webOS is based on Alpine, but that LG has not provided sufficiently useful GPL source materials for rebuilding or customizing components.

news.title: Vizio network traffic is being examined for smart-TV data collection
news.summary: One speaker says they are currently capturing network traffic from Vizio TVs and describes the findings as disturbing, without specifying what the traffic contains. The discussion also characterizes Vizio's advertising business as a major source of its TV economics.

news.title: Linux desktop market-share growth remains difficult to measure
news.summary: The speakers discuss claims that some reported Linux market-share growth may come from Linux-based bots rather than human desktop users. They say Cloudflare attributes its observed increase to bots and agents, while Steam and other signals suggest human Linux use is rising but remains in the single-digit percentages.

news.title: China's move away from Windows could spur development of domestic Linux systems
news.summary: The speakers say China has had Linux operating systems for years, citing Kylin OS and systems paired with Zhaoxin CPUs, but that the new government push could lead to more active development. They expect this to expand work on operating systems and the surrounding software ecosystem.

news.title: A locally installed open-source bookkeeping tool is being used as a QuickBooks replacement
news.summary: A speaker says they replaced QuickBooks with a bookkeeping application developed largely by one person, with much of its code open source. They value that it runs locally and does not communicate with servers, and say it avoids about $1,500 per year in QuickBooks fees.

news.title: Open-source software projects are emerging as alternatives to proprietary creative tools
news.summary: The speakers describe testing an open-source Photoshop-like application as a possible replacement for Adobe Photoshop, which they say is a major reason one of them still uses Windows on a laptop. They also mention projects that make existing software more familiar through themes and matching keyboard shortcuts.

news.title: Linux kernel 7.2 adds USB stream support
news.summary: The transcript describes a new Linux kernel 7.2 feature called USB stream, presented as another option for transferring data over USB4. The speaker says it may enable a purpose-built interface for VLM clustering, but that use is still being evaluated.

news.title: Thunderbolt networking is being used for direct machine-to-machine links on Linux
news.summary: The speaker reports setting up a direct Thunderbolt 4 connection between a Ryzen AI Halo system and a Minisforum N5 NAS, using it as a dedicated 20 Gbit link separate from Ethernet. They say current Linux support is easier and more stable than before, and their testing found lower latency than the Ethernet connection.

news.title: Thunderbolt links can support clustering and Proxmox workload migration
news.summary: The direct Thunderbolt connection is being tested as a high-speed link for clustering, including AI workloads, and for a Proxmox cluster. The speaker says it could also carry VM migrations between machines without using the Ethernet network.

news.title: Kernel 7.2 USB stream clustering setup requires bleeding-edge software
news.summary: The Ryzen AI Halo ships with kernel 6, which the speaker says is too old for the USB stream approach; their demonstration uses a release candidate for kernel 7.2. The Thunderbolt networking setup, by contrast, does not require the new kernel.

news.title: Wildcat Lake laptop audio support backported to Linux kernel 7.1
news.summary: The presenter backported working audio support from kernel 7.2 to kernel 7.1 for the Chewy Core 3 laptop, which uses Intel Wildcat Lake. A forum thread provides configuration instructions, and a DKMS version of the driver was published on GitHub; the driver will not work on kernel 6.

news.title: Looking Glass adds signed Windows indirect display driver and HDR support
news.summary: Looking Glass is described as feature complete, with a signed official Windows indirect display driver that removes the need for a dummy plug or a separately connected monitor. It supports HDR and resolutions up to 5120×440 at 120 fps, with the presenter reporting less than one millisecond of display latency.

news.title: Rui Carmo develops a Wayland-based remote desktop implementation for Linux
news.summary: The presenter highlighted Rui Carmo's GitHub projects, including an implementation of remote desktop on top of Wayland. The project is presented as an alternative to existing approaches that either require an already logged-in GNOME session or create a separate session through XRDP.

news.title: Rui Carmo publishes agent-related projects and Linux kernel mailing-list coding skill
news.summary: Rui Carmo has also been working on agentic client projects, including PyClaw-related work. Separately, someone turned examples from Linus Torvalds's email history into an importable agent skill intended to teach agents his coding preferences for kernel patches and mailing-list messages.

news.title: Ryzen AI Halo setup demonstrates USB4 networking and DMA transfers
news.summary: The presenter reported that DMA transfers over USB4 at 20 Gbit are nearly working on a Ryzen AI Halo setup, while Thunderbolt networking is fully operational. A how-to guide for Thunderbolt networking is available on the forum.

news.title: Presenter runs a highly available home-lab cluster across Strix Halo and N5 systems
news.summary: The presenter described a cluster in which AI tasks run on a Strix Halo system and virtual machines run on an N5, with critical VMs mirrored between the two machines. Media VMs and workloads on mechanical storage remain on the N5.

news.title: ASRock sends 10th-anniversary Taichi motherboard for an AM5 build
news.summary: ASRock sent the presenter a motherboard marking Taichi's 10th anniversary, and he plans to build an AM5 system around it. The board has built-in 10-gigabit Ethernet and a 24+2+1-phase design; the planned build will reuse an AMD-supplied 950 X3D2 processor and include low-latency G.Skill memory and Kioxia storage.

news.title: Eric Raymond says the New Hacker's Dictionary helped build a coalition against internet censorship
news.summary: Raymond said he edited and published The New Hacker's Dictionary in 1990 as part of an effort to build a coalition against internet censorship. He said the book also drew readers into hacker culture, helping set the stage for the later open-source movement.

news.title: Raymond says an early Idrisil CD-ROM introduced him to Linux
news.summary: Raymond recalled receiving a CD-ROM from Idrisil in 1993, buying a CD-ROM drive to run it, and finding the operating system better than the System V system he was using. Studying why it worked so well led him to develop ideas about open-source development.

news.title: Raymond says open-source development challenged the prevailing view of Brooks's law
news.summary: Raymond said software engineering thinking at the time was dominated by Brooks's law, which predicted that adding developers would increase communication problems and lead to project failure. He described his work as making Linux developers aware of the collaborative method they were using.

news.title: Raymond urges right-to-repair advocates to frame device ownership as a matter of freedom
news.summary: Raymond argued that advocates should make a broad moral case that people should control the things they own, rather than present repair only as a right that lawmakers might grant. He said people do not want to be controlled by tools they bought to serve them.

news.title: Raymond warns that digital controls and intellectual-property law obstruct repair and preservation
news.summary: Raymond said vendors use technical controls and intellectual-property law to obstruct activities including device repair, format shifting, and video-game preservation. He characterized these restrictions as threats to users' control over digital culture.

news.title: Raymond says hacker-community cohesion helped defeat the Communications Decency Act
news.summary: Raymond said his participation as an individual amicus in the Supreme Court challenge to the Communications Decency Act was one part of the effort against it. He also credited a more cohesive hacker culture, willing to speak up for shared interests, with helping create the political climate for the CDA's defeat.

news.title: Raymond recommends using journalists to explain the real-world effects of technology restrictions
news.summary: Raymond said advocates can enlist journalists and other communicators to show that measures such as device controls and identity requirements are not merely technical details, but can affect people in their everyday lives.

news.title: Raymond describes fear, profit, and status as tactics used to promote open source
news.summary: Raymond said he appealed to businesses' fear of dependence on closed-source vendors, their desire for greater profits, and people's interest in social status to promote open source. He argued that vendor dependencies can leave businesses subject to changes on the vendor's schedule and increasing user control.

news.title: Interview raises concern that age-verification campaigns could shield platforms from liability
news.summary: The interviewer said Meta and similar companies fund age-verification campaigns as a way to avoid legal liability for what children do on their platforms. The discussion connected this concern to government-backed age-verification requirements, but did not provide further evidence or details.

news.title: FCC adds foreign-produced consumer routers to its covered list
news.summary: The FCC added foreign-produced consumer routers to its covered list, citing unacceptable national-security and cybersecurity risks. The transcript describes this as the router-ban development and says it has prompted security audits of routers.

news.title: Level1Techs uses a local AI-agent workflow to assist Wi-Fi 7 router testing
news.summary: Level1Techs describes using Turnstone, a locally run agent harness, to help manage repetitive Wi-Fi 7 testing tasks such as checking logs, validating files, comparing runs, and flagging anomalies. The agents assist with defined tools and scripts; they do not benchmark routers themselves, and their actions and outputs are auditable.

news.title: Turnstone provides permissions, workstreams, and audit logs for local agents
news.summary: Turnstone is presented as an orchestration layer that gives agents controlled access to tools, records commands and outputs, and preserves artifacts for inspection. Its workflow checks that expected files and parser fields exist and can compare results with a previous known-good run.

news.title: Level1Techs runs local inference on a system with 128 GB of VRAM
news.summary: The Turnstone workflow uses local inference on a machine described as having 128 GB of VRAM. The presenter says the work can also be done on two GPUs, though more slowly and with less parallelism.

news.title: Level1Techs ports its Wi-Fi testing tools to Python 3
news.summary: The presenter says older testing utilities, including scripts written in Python 2, were ported to Python 3. The scripts provide explicit, narrowly defined operations for the agent-assisted testing workflow.

news.title: Level1Techs reports a Netgear router service can enable SSH via a UDP port 22 magic packet
news.summary: The presenter says a security audit found a secret service on a Netgear router that enables SSH when sent a magic packet on UDP port 22. The transcript does not identify the router model or provide further technical details.

news.title: Netgear GPL firmware archives reportedly disappeared from its website
news.summary: The presenter says Netgear's GPL firmware archives have disappeared from the company's website amid scrutiny related to the router-ban issue. No explanation from Netgear is provided in the transcript.

news.title: Level1Techs expands router security audits alongside Wi-Fi 7 reviews
news.summary: Level1Techs says its router reviews now include security audits in addition to performance testing. The audits use scripts to inventory services, inspect firmware versions and components, and check whether changes or patches are reflected in results.

news.title: Razer officially supports Linux on the Blade 18
news.summary: Razer is officially supporting Ubuntu 24.04 on the Blade 18. The reviewer reports that most hardware works on Linux, while noting that newer kernels and security updates may be needed and that suspend/resume remains problematic in testing.

news.title: Blade 18 BIOS exposes Secure Boot controls and custom key enrollment
news.summary: The Blade 18 BIOS provides an option to disable Secure Boot and supports enrolling custom keys for kernel signing. The reviewer also successfully enrolled a key to boot Ventoy.

news.title: Thunderbolt 5 works on the Blade 18 with Linux kernel 7.0.3
news.summary: The Blade 18's Thunderbolt 5 port worked with boltctl on kernel 7.0.3, and the reviewer reports that Linux handles the laptop's separate Thunderbolt 4 and Thunderbolt 5 controllers. A Thunderbolt 5 dock with an external RTX 6000 also worked plug-and-play.

news.title: Blade 18 suspend/resume can leave the graphics session unusable
news.summary: On the tested Linux setup, waking the Blade 18 sometimes left only a blinking cursor; attempting to restart the display manager or switch to a graphical console could hard-lock the machine. The reviewer could not resolve the issue with BIOS settings and suspected an Nvidia graphics problem, while saying the laptop worked with Razer's Ubuntu LTS setup.

news.title: Razer Blade 18 supports up to 128 GB of non-ECC memory
news.summary: The reviewer tested a 128 GB memory configuration in the Blade 18, including with an RTX 5090, but ECC UDIMMs did not work. Razer offers configurations with up to 128 GB, though the reviewer noted that some 128 GB kits may have higher CAS latency than lower-capacity configurations.

news.title: Linux battery life on the Blade 18 exceeded six hours in light use
news.summary: The reviewer reported more than six hours of battery life on Linux during light web browsing, better than Windows in the same general use case. The BIOS also includes an 80% battery charge limit intended to help preserve battery health.

news.title: Blade 18 BIOS includes an 80% battery charge limit
news.summary: Razer added a BIOS setting that caps battery charging at 80%. The reviewer said the limit can help preserve battery life and reduce the risk of battery swelling.

news.title: Linux sensor-monitoring package is being developed and tested on the Blade 18
news.summary: The reviewer said Level1Techs' sensor-monitoring package, Simon, is in late alpha or early beta and can monitor power use and CPU and GPU clock speeds on the Blade 18. Testing the laptop helped with the package's debugging.

news.title: LM Studio runs Nvidia local AI models on the Blade 18
news.summary: LM Studio worked with the Nvidia proprietary drivers on Linux. The reviewer reported about 17 tokens per second for a 27–35-billion-parameter model on the laptop's mobile RTX 5090, and about 120 tokens per second using an external GPU through a Thunderbolt 5 dock.

news.title: Razer Core X V2 Thunderbolt enclosure supports four-slot GPUs
news.summary: The reviewer highlighted Razer's Core X V2, an external Thunderbolt 5 GPU enclosure that can accommodate a four-slot graphics card and uses a user-supplied power supply. The enclosure was described as a straightforward design for external GPUs.

news.title: S Info Linux hardware-monitoring project is nearing release
news.summary: S Info is an open-source, single static Rust binary for Linux hardware information and real-time sensor monitoring, covering CPUs, motherboards, GPUs, USB, batteries, PCIe, and other devices. The project is not yet live, but the developer expects it to be published after a few days of cleanup.

news.title: S Info reads Threadripper motherboard sensors that were difficult to access with LM Sensors
news.summary: The developer demonstrated S Info collecting extensive telemetry on Threadripper systems, including ASUS EC and Nuvoton NCT6799 sensor data that they could not obtain through ordinary LM Sensors installation. Some voltage-conversion labels still need work, but temperature, fan, power, and other readings are available.

news.title: S Info combines telemetry from multiple Linux hardware interfaces
news.summary: The demonstrated tool gathers information from sources including HSMP, hwmon, AMD GPU interfaces, network hardware, IPMI, NVML, and motherboard Super I/O sensors. It also reports PCIe device details and supports collapsible groups, configurable threshold alerts, label customization, and HTML reports.

news.title: S Info warns that direct I²C sensor probing carries some risk
news.summary: S Info directly probes I²C-connected sensor controllers, in a manner compared to LM Sensors, and the developer said this creates a small amount of risk. A warning about the behavior is planned for the project README.

news.title: S Info will use text-based motherboard label databases
news.summary: The project plans to keep board-specific sensor labels in simple text files so contributors can add motherboard mappings without editing complicated source code. The approach is intended to make sensor labeling easier to maintain and more forward-compatible, following a model the developer also described for DIM labels in Rasdaemon.

news.title: S Info plans additional PCIe, logging, and alert features
news.summary: The developer said future work may add PCIe speed information and further logging and alert capabilities. These were described as planned ideas rather than features already completed.

news.title: Intel B60 supports seven SR-IOV virtual functions in the demonstrated setup
news.summary: The presenter said Intel's B60, a 24 GB graphics card, can run seven virtual functions. They contrasted this with the B50, whose most up-to-date official driver was said to support only two virtual functions, and described B60 SR-IOV as more stable.

news.title: Turnstone AI orchestration project is available on GitHub
news.summary: Turnstone, described as a multi-node AI orchestration platform, is live in the Turnstone Labs GitHub repository and can be cloned and run with Docker Compose. It can use local models or cloud APIs and is intended to coordinate AI-assisted tasks across machines and tools.

news.title: Turnstone uses approval controls and container isolation for command execution
news.summary: Turnstone can call tools to execute commands, with approval required for commands that are not pre-approved. The presenter demonstrated its web interface running commands in a container and said its command-line mode can execute as the user; the project also supports custom tools and human review of proposed actions.

news.title: Turnstone supports multiple model providers and persistent task context
news.summary: The project can work with local models and cloud providers, and its repository includes support for multiple nodes and model providers, plus Discord and Slack plugins. The presenter said important information can persist across sessions using PostgreSQL or SQLite.

news.title: Kappa fine-tune targets tool use and long-context recall
news.summary: Kappa is a fine-tune of GPT-OSS-20B intended to improve tool calling and long-context recall for system-administration tasks. The presenter said it has a 131K context length, scored 100% across the shown RULER long-context benchmark results, uses MXFP4, and can run on GPUs with 10 GB of VRAM.

news.title: Kappa was trained with Dungeons & Dragons-style character alignment
news.summary: The Kappa model was trained with Dungeons & Dragons-style character alignment, including a lawful-evil persona described as favoring malicious compliance. The presenter said this training makes the model less sycophantic and more likely to push back on requests it considers unwise.

news.title: Turnstone and Kappa are being used to automate hardware testing and administration
news.summary: The developer said Turnstone and Kappa helped accelerate S Info development by coordinating tests across machines and handling hardware-specific procedures. They also demonstrated using a documented tool workflow to prepare a MikroTik switch-port reconfiguration while presenting the proposed changes for human review.

news.title: A weekly Linux-focused show is planned
news.summary: The presenter said they want to make a recurring Linux-focused weekly show covering news, hardware, drivers, projects, and practical productivity topics. A forum thread will host the agenda and community questions, with the format intended to avoid getting bogged down in general controversy.

news.title: Presenter plans GTC coverage and a Spark giveaway
news.summary: The presenter said they would attend NVIDIA GTC the following week, with NVIDIA providing a ticket, and planned to make content with Supermicro. They also announced a giveaway of an NVIDIA Spark and directed viewers to the forum for details.

news.title: Proxmox 9 guide updated for Intel Flex GPU SR-IOV
news.summary: A forum guide for configuring Intel Flex 140 and Flex 170 GPUs with SR-IOV on Proxmox 9 has been updated. The revised procedure uses a Proxmox 9 host with kernel 6.14.8 and is described as requiring fewer steps than the older approach.

news.title: Intel expands documentation and backport support for Flex GPU drivers
news.summary: Intel has updated its SR-IOV documentation for Ubuntu, SUSE Linux Enterprise, and Red Hat, and provides an out-of-tree i915 DKMS driver for backporting to supported kernels. Its driver repository has also consolidated the previous Ubuntu-specific fork into the backport/main branch.

news.title: Flex GPU SR-IOV support varies sharply across kernel versions
news.summary: Testing found that Intel's out-of-tree i915 DKMS driver can build on older kernels, but kernel 6.8 breaks the Flex GPU setup while kernel 6.14.8 works in the demonstrated Proxmox configuration. The presenter also cautioned that other kernel versions, including 6.14.11 in their testing, may behave differently depending on driver and firmware versions.

news.title: Intel's firmware repository does not clearly include Flex card firmware
news.summary: Intel provides a firmware repository, but the presenter could not find the lower-level firmware needed by some Flex 140 cards there. Updating that card firmware requires the XPU SMI utility, and older cards may arrive with firmware that causes setup problems.

news.title: XPU SMI supports Flex GPU management and virtual-function creation
news.summary: Intel's XPU SMI utility can query installed cards, update firmware, and create GPU virtual functions. The Proxmox setup uses it to configure SR-IOV instances, with the number of instances constrained by the card and affecting the VRAM available to each one.

news.title: Proxmox PCIe-bridge handling can prevent VFIO binding
news.summary: The presenter describes a longstanding Proxmox issue in which its device-binding logic does not look far enough down the PCIe tree for devices behind a bridge, preventing correct VFIO binding. A custom helper script and systemd service are used to create Flex GPU virtual functions and bind them to VFIO at boot.

news.title: StrongTZ repository is not seeking to maintain Flex GPU support
news.summary: The presenter says the StrongTZ out-of-tree i915 project, previously used for this functionality, does not want to support Intel Flex data-center GPUs. The newer Intel driver work may reduce the need for outside maintenance, though the presenter invited community members to help test and maintain Flex support.

news.title: Flex 140 test system ran 18 virtual machines with GPU acceleration
news.summary: In a demonstration using a Flex 140 in a 32-core, 64-thread Zen 3 server with 256 GB of memory, 18 virtual machines were running while a VM achieved 115 FPS in the Heaven benchmark. The presenter noted that CPU resources were oversubscribed but the workload ran acceptably when the CPUs were not handling graphics acceleration.

news.title: Intel B50 GPU SR-IOV works with Proxmox 9 virtual machines
news.summary: A B50 GPU with 16 GB of memory was used to provide SR-IOV GPU acceleration to multiple VMs on Proxmox 9. The setup ran for 48 hours without major hiccups, demonstrating a GPU-accelerated virtual desktop use case.

news.title: B50 SR-IOV configuration supports multiple GPU instances, with current driver limits
news.summary: The B50 can be divided into GPU instances, including four 4 GB slices or eight 2 GB instances in the tested setup. Although the configuration appears to support up to 12 instances, the presenter could not get 12 working with the current driver.

news.title: B50 SR-IOV instances show unusual performance interactions
news.summary: GPU performance in one SR-IOV instance can change when another instance places demands on the GPU, unlike the hard partitioning behavior the presenter observed with the Flex 170. The presenter also reported that moving a Heaven benchmark window off-screen and back could raise its frame rate from about 20 FPS to roughly 120–130 FPS, which was attributed to a likely driver bug.

news.title: Older Intel Xe graphics driver performed better in B50 SR-IOV testing
news.summary: Testing two versions of the Xe graphics driver found that the older version worked somewhat better for this use case. The newer version was described as slightly less stable.

news.title: OBS encoding was not working in the tested B50 SR-IOV setup
news.summary: The presenter reported that OBS could not use Intel's encoding facilities in the current setup. Encoding was identified as a part of the driver functionality that was not working.

news.title: Proxmox B50 SR-IOV setup requires a custom 6.17 kernel and patches
news.summary: The setup requires building a custom Linux 6.17 kernel for Proxmox, with patches primarily related to AppArmor. A forum contributor published Debian packages on GitHub, while the presenter said they had disabled AppArmor for their own experimentation.

news.title: B50 SR-IOV setup instructions and testing discussion published on forum
news.summary: A how-to for enabling SR-IOV on the B50 under Proxmox 9 was posted on the Level1Techs forum. The presenter directed users to the forum thread for evolving instructions, driver findings, and discussion.

news.title: GMKtec offers a 64GB Strix Halo mini PC configuration
news.summary: The reviewed GMKtec Strix Halo system is available with 64GB of memory and a 1TB SSD, for about $500 less than the 128GB configuration. Its memory is shared between the system and integrated GPU, and the 64GB model can run models up to around 30 billion parameters comfortably, according to the review.

news.title: GMKtec's Strix Halo mini PC supports configurable power and hardware settings
news.summary: GMKtec configures the Strix Halo system to run at up to about 140 watts, while its unlocked BIOS lets users lower the power limit to 110 or 120 watts. The BIOS also provides fan and RGB controls and settings for an OCuLink breakout adapter.

news.title: Linux gaming on Strix Halo approaches Windows performance
news.summary: The review found that Linux gaming performance on the GMKtec Strix Halo system was close to Windows performance, with several tested games running at playable frame rates. The reviewer said recent Linux distributions with current kernels and Mesa versions provide a strong experience on the platform.

news.title: Ubuntu 25.04 installer includes improvements for Strix Halo
news.summary: The reviewer said the Ubuntu 25.04 installer available around early August 2025 included updates and quality-of-life improvements for the Strix Halo platform. CachyOS and Bazzite were also identified as Linux options that can provide a ready-to-use gaming setup.

news.title: Omarchy Linux distribution is presented as an option for experimenting with workflow choices
news.summary: The reviewer highlighted Omarchy, associated with the founder of 37signals and Basecamp, as an opinionated Linux distribution that makes choices about window management and keyboard shortcuts for users. It was recommended as a way to explore a different Linux workflow.

news.title: Framework offers an ITX desktop built around AMD’s Ryzen AI Max+ 395
news.summary: Framework’s Desktop uses an ITX motherboard with AMD’s 16-core Ryzen AI Max+ 395 APU and up to 128 GB of unified memory. The system is also available with 64 GB and 32 GB configurations, and the motherboard can be installed in other ITX cases.

news.title: Framework Desktop motherboard includes high-speed I/O and a PCIe expansion slot
news.summary: The board provides 5-gigabit Ethernet, dual USB 4, HDMI, DisplayPort, two PCIe Gen 4 M.2 slots with heatsinks, and a PCIe Gen 4 x4 slot with 25 watts of power delivery. The Desktop case does not leave practical room to use the x4 slot, but other ITX cases can.

news.title: Framework Desktop supports Linux distributions including Bazzite, Ubuntu, and Fedora
news.summary: Framework supports Linux on the Desktop, including Bazzite, Ubuntu, and Fedora. The reviewer also tested Arch-based systems and highlighted CachyOS as an easier-to-install option with gaming-oriented defaults.

news.title: AMD’s Ryzen AI Max+ 395 delivers near-desktop Zen 5 CPU performance in a 140-watt envelope
news.summary: The 16-core Zen 5 processor is reported to reach roughly 80–90% of a Ryzen 9 9950X’s performance in single- and multithreaded workloads. Its quad-channel unified memory provides about 200 GB/s of bandwidth, while the platform has 12 PCIe Gen 4 lanes for its M.2 and x4 connections.

news.title: Ryzen AI Max+ 395’s integrated Radeon 8060S offers strong Linux gaming performance
news.summary: The integrated Radeon 8060S is described as roughly comparable to an RTX 4060, with 1440p gaming at 60 fps and 1080p gaming presented as achievable. The reviewer reports that Linux graphics support works well and that Helldivers 2 performed better on Linux than on Windows in testing.

news.title: Linux drivers let the Radeon 8060S use unified memory dynamically for graphics
news.summary: In testing, MangoHud showed only 512 MB of VRAM reserved rather than a large fixed allocation. The system can draw additional graphics memory from the 128 GB unified-memory pool as needed, which the reviewer attributed to recent Linux driver and AMD platform support.

news.title: Framework Desktop’s memory is not upgradeable, making the 32 GB model a constrained option
news.summary: The system’s unified memory is soldered and cannot be upgraded. The reviewer considered 64 GB a suitable workstation and gaming configuration, while warning that 32 GB may be limiting over the long term and recommending buyers focus on the 64 GB or 128 GB versions.

news.title: Vulkan enables day-one support for a 120-billion-parameter model on the Radeon 8060S
news.summary: The reviewer reports running OpenAI’s newly released 120-billion-parameter model on the platform through the Vulkan backend without modifications on its release day. In testing, Vulkan matched or outperformed other options and reached about 33 tokens per second.

news.title: AMD ROCm support for RDNA has improved, but remains less turnkey than Vulkan
news.summary: The reviewer says ROCm support for RDNA GPUs such as the Radeon 8060S has advanced substantially over the previous six months, though ROCm is designed primarily for AMD CDNA GPUs and still requires setup and troubleshooting. Framework forum posts and the ROCm GitHub issue tracker are cited as resources for configuration and performance information.

news.title: USB 4 or OCuLink can connect the Framework system to an external Nvidia GPU for AI workloads
news.summary: The reviewer demonstrated pairing the system with an Nvidia SFF-4000 Ada GPU with 20 GB of VRAM over USB 4 or OCuLink. The combined setup can divide model workloads between AMD compute and Nvidia, and was described as providing 148 GB of total memory capacity for running very large models.

news.title: Framework Desktop includes a 50-TOPS NPU
news.summary: The Ryzen AI Max+ 395 platform includes a 50-TOPS neural processing unit, which the reviewer identified as another potential compute resource alongside the CPU and integrated GPU.

news.title: Framework’s BIOS is praised as the strongest among Strix Halo platforms
news.summary: The reviewer described Framework’s BIOS as the best put-together BIOS among the Strix Halo platforms they had encountered. The BIOS is part of Framework’s own platform implementation.

news.title: PhotoCraft releases an AI-assisted open-source Photoshop reimplementation
news.summary: Arcraft has published PhotoCraft on GitHub, describing it as a clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop written almost entirely in Rust and developed with AI agents. The transcript estimates it reproduces roughly 60–70% of Photoshop's functionality, while noting that workflows, tools, and features remain incomplete.

news.title: PhotoCraft exposes shared commands through UI, CLI, JSON, and MCP
news.summary: PhotoCraft is designed for both people and agents: its menus, tools, and dialogs invoke commands from a registry of more than 500 commands. The UI, CLI, JSON control channel, and MCP server use the same commands, and the project reportedly tests its output against results generated by Photoshop.

news.title: An open-source Rust project reimplements Adobe Premiere workflows
news.summary: A separate clean-room open-source reimplementation of Adobe Premiere, also written in Rust, has been made available on GitHub. The project aims to reproduce Premiere's familiar workflows and compatibility, though the transcript does not specify its feature completeness.

news.title: An open-source Rust project reimplements Adobe Lightroom
news.summary: The transcript reports a third clean-room open-source reimplementation of an Adobe application: a Lightroom alternative written in Rust. It is presented as part of the same wave of AI-assisted software replication, but no specific feature-completeness estimate is given for it.
